title: Love was his meaning (Revelations 86)
hookLine: after long pondering, the answer: love was his meaning
tomorrow: is knowing the right answer the same as living it?

cards: A lyric can sit in your head for a long time before it lands, some ordinary afternoon, and suddenly you know what it meant.
Julian of Norwich has written down what she was shown: a hazelnut in her palm, a servant in a ditch, a mother who feeds her child with herself.

In her final chapter she admits she kept wanting to know what her Lord meant by all of it. She asked, often, and she doesn't hide that the waiting was long. And long after the showings, she says, an answer came.

teach.b: It comes as a conversation inside her. Would you know your Lord's meaning in this? Know it well.
"Love was His meaning." Then three quick questions, and the same reply each time. Who showed it to you?
Love. What did he show you? Love.
Why did he show it? For love. Not a theory, not a rule: a who, a what and a why, all answered the same.
It would fit on a sticky note.

Then a gentle warning: hold on to this and you'll understand more of the same, but you'll never find anything else in it. There's no hidden second meaning under the love. And she looks back to the very start.
We had a beginning when we were made, she says, but the love God made us with had no beginning at all. Read her book in that light. The hazelnut lasts because it's loved.
The servant in the ditch is looked on with love. The asking starts with him. The mother feeds her child out of love.
And the week does the same: Francis taking the brothers he was given, Clare gazing into a mirror, Julian asking, and asking, and hearing one word back.
Here's the one to tell a friend: a book of visions ends not with a secret, but with one plain word.

how: Some Christians read Revelations of Divine Love slowly, a chapter at a time, as part of their prayer, and come back to its last chapter.

games.q: what does “love was his meaning” mean?
o: Julian's answer: love was the point of all she saw
a medieval saying that love is life's only goal
a line meaning God's love is always easy to see

games.q: love was his meaning — tap the pairs.
p: the love we were made with

s: Julian understood her showings the moment she saw them
she says she kept asking what they meant, and the answer came long after.
Julian is told she will never find any other meaning in it but love
hold on to this, she hears, and you'll understand more of the same, never anything else.
a mystic's book like Julian's ends with a secret for insiders
the popular picture. hers ends with one plain word, love, asked and answered three ways.

games.q: a friend reading Julian says 'love was his meaning' must be a cover for some deeper secret. what does Julian's own last page say?
o: he's right; the real meaning is hidden in the hazelnut.
she's warned she'll never find anything else in it.
she says the meaning changes for every reader.
games.why: hold on to this, Julian hears, and you'll understand more of the same, but never anything else in it. no secret under the love.

practice: Run back over your day so far like a film. Count on your fingers three moments where love showed up, small is fine: a text, a held door, a meal. Stay with the last one, and ask Julian's questions of it: who showed it, and why?

wordCard.voice: Love was his meaning. The answer Julian heard, long after her showings, to what all of them had meant: love, and nothing else.

carryVoice: Your line: love was his meaning, and who showed it, what, and why came back love every time. That's the week, done.
